title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Stellar AI
summary: Redwood AE + SE ran a renewal and expansion check-in with Stellar AI. Customer interested in upgrading to dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, enabling EU region, and extending contract for 12 months to lock pricing. SE discussed performance and KV cache behavior, quantization options, and recommended benchmarking steps. Security questions focused on SOC 2, SSO/SAML, and KMS integration. Agreed next steps: share updated pricing, run a focused benchmark (sample prompts + perf spreadsheet), share SOC2 & security docs, draft SOW for extension and capacity add-on.
next_steps: Redwood to send updated pricing for 12-month renewal + Dedicated capacity by 2027-03-03
SE to schedule benchmark run and share perf spreadsheet by 2027-03-07
Redwood Security to share SOC2 report and KMS integration guide by 2027-03-04
Draft SOW for capacity add-on and EU region deployment by 2027-03-10
action_items: Maya Chen: send pricing and renewal draft (due 2027-03-03)
Ethan Ross: run benchmark on existing workload, share results & spreadsheet (due 2027-03-07)
Lena Park: coordinate SSO/KMS scoping call with Marco (due 2027-03-04)
Priya Kapoor: provide representative prompt set and traffic profile (due 2027-03-02)
Daniel Ortiz: confirm compliance reviewer contact for SOC2 questions (due 2027-03-05)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Lena - Redwood; Priya, Daniel, Sara, Marco - Stellar AI

Summary (auto): renewal and expansion discussion; capacity and region add; security questions; agreed next steps.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate ya, uh just to kick off this is our renewal & expansion check-in for Stellar, how's everyone doing?
00:08 Priya Kapoor: good thanks, busy week but excited to chat, we've got a few pressing items around scaling and region parity for EU customers.
00:15 Ethan Ross: cool yea, the plan from our side is to walk through Dedicated capacity options, performance expectations, and the EU rollout timeline. we'll also cover any security or procurement blockers.
00:26 Sara Nguyen: top line we want to lock pricing for 12 months if possible and add capacity for our busiest pipelines.
00:32 Maya Chen: perfect, that aligns with what we saw in usage — Priya you can correct me — your token volumes spiked in Q4 and current hosted capacity is near burst limits?
00:45 Priya Kapoor: yep exact, we saw peak bursts during model retrain windows and during demo events; the latency p95 rose and it's affecting UX.
00:54 Marco Li: and for EU we need data residency; we can't route certain PII outside region so region parity is must.
01:02 Ethan Ross: got it. so for capacity we recommend a Dedicated pool reserved with burst capacity; it gives predictable throughput and isolates KV cache behavior to reduce tail latency. to be clear though, Dedicated has a commit model — you pay for reserved nodes but get predictable SLOs.
01:20 Daniel Ortiz: curious on quantization: can we get the cost down while keeping LLM quality? we run reranking and generation.
01:28 Ethan Ross: yes you can — we have quantization profiles that typically reduce GPU memory and token cost; for reranking we suggest int8 for the smaller models, mixed-precision for generation. there's a tradeoff, you'll want to test on your prompt set.
01:40 Priya Kapoor: that's the thing, we need a benchmark on our prompts. can Redwood run a focused perf test?
01:46 Maya Chen: absolutely. Ethan can run a benchmark with your prompt set — we usually collect a representative sample, run under a similar QPS, and produce a perf spreadsheet with latency percentiles and cost estimates.
02:00 Priya Kapoor: great. timeline?
02:03 Maya Chen: if you can share prompts and traffic profile by next Tuesday (2027-03-02) we can run and have results by 2027-03-07.
02:12 Priya Kapoor: yes that works. I'll assign Daniel to collect them.
02:16 Daniel Ortiz: noted.
02:18 Sara Nguyen: on contract length, we prefer 12 months at slightly discounted rate if we commit to dedicated capacity. what are typical discount bands?
02:27 Maya Chen: for a 12-month reserved capacity we can do a blended discount depending on commit size; I'll send an updated pricing sheet after this call. approximate ranges are 10-18% depending on capacity and optional add-ons like extended retention or premium SLA.
02:42 Marco Li: we need to confirm EU region latency. do you have EU regions live for our powered model?
02:48 Ethan Ross: we do. hosted EU regions are available and we can provision Dedicated capacity in EU (subject to capacity schedule). there's also an onboarding step for Private/VPC if you want customer-managed network.
02:59 Marco Li: for now we prefer Redwood-managed EU Dedicated in our tenancy, as long as KMS and audit logs meet our security bar.
03:07 Lena Park: to confirm, we support KMS integrations (customer-managed keys) and provide audit logs; we'll share SOC2 and security docs after this call.
03:16 Priya Kapoor: perfect. we have a compliance team who will review SOC2 and the KMS flow. does Redwood encrypt at rest with customer keys?
03:24 Lena Park: yes, we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via supported KMS providers; we also have application-layer encryption for sensitive fields as needed.
03:35 Daniel Ortiz: any gotchas with SSO? SAML or OIDC? we use SAML with Okta.
03:40 Maya Chen: SAML + Okta is supported; we've onboarded multiple customers with that flow. we'll include a SSO setup doc.
03:47 Priya Kapoor: good. procurement wise we might need standard security attestation and an updated DPA for the EU.
03:54 Maya Chen: understood, we'll surface our DPA and data residency notes.
03:58 Ethan Ross: back to perf — one more detail on KV cache: with Dedicated we can pin large KV caches per model instance which reduces repeated prefix compute and helps p95. if you have long conversation histories that's especially helpful.
04:12 Priya Kapoor: we do, conversation history for support agents is long, so that could help.
04:18 Daniel Ortiz: pricing question — if we scale to multiple regions, how does billing work? single bill with region breakdown?
04:25 Maya Chen: you get a unified invoice with per-region usage breakout; reserved Dedicated capacity can be allocated per region and we can show per-route cost.
04:33 Sara Nguyen: ok procurement timing — we need an internal signoff by March 20 to hit our release window.
04:38 Maya Chen: sounds feasible. we'll aim to get pricing and SOW draft early March.
04:42 Priya Kapoor: anything else on technical risk? latency vs cost tradeoffs?
04:46 Ethan Ross: main risk is model size + sequence length; longer sequences increase compute nonlinearly. strategies: truncation, caching, batching windows, or switching to mixed-precision kernels. Dedicated helps by giving you predictability so the autoscaler won't evict capacity during peaks.
05:03 Marco Li: wanted to raise one more thing — can we have a canary during region rollout to validate latency?
05:09 Ethan Ross: yes, we do canary and A/B routing; we can route a percentage of traffic to EU region and measure. rollbacks are automated if SLOs breach.
05:18 Priya Kapoor: that gives comfort.
05:20 Maya Chen: cool, so to recap: Priya will send prompt set and traffic profile by 2027-03-02; Ethan will run perf and return spreadsheet by 2027-03-07; Maya will send pricing and renewal draft by 2027-03-03; Lena will share SOC2 and KMS guide by 2027-03-04; Redwood and Stellar to plan SOW for Dedicated + EU region (target draft 2027-03-10). any additions?
05:42 Sara Nguyen: please include cost delta for int8 vs fp16 and how quality regression is measured.
05:47 Ethan Ross: noted, we'll include quality baseline and eval metrics per prompt set.
05:51 Daniel Ortiz: i'll confirm internal compliance contact.
05:54 Priya Kapoor: thanks everyone.
05:56 Maya Chen: great thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and action items; chat after.

(End of transcript)
